nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the binary run lengths of $n$ form the list of the lengths of the maximal runs of $1$s in the binary expansion of $n$, in the order in which the runs occur when the digits are read from the least significant one. This is the paper's list $\mathcal{L}(n)$, whose order does not matter there; for $n = 0$ the list is empty.
nodes.title: Binary run lengths

nodes.summary: Given a list $b_1, \dots, b_k$ of natural numbers (binary digits) and a natural number $c$, this is the list, in order of occurrence, of the lengths of the maximal runs of $1$s in the sequence consisting of $c$ ones followed by $b_1, \dots, b_k$, where every digit other than $1$ ends a run.
nodes.title: Run lengths of a digit list

nodes.summary: Let $r$ be a natural number, let $d_0, \dots, d_r$ be integers, and let $S : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$ satisfy $S(0) = 1$ and $S(m + 1) = d_0 S(m) + d_1 S(m - 1) + \dots + d_r S(m - r)$ for every $m \ge r$. Let $\gamma(1)$ be the $(r + 1) \times (r + 1)$ integer matrix with rows and columns indexed by $0, \dots, r$ whose row $i < r$ has a $1$ in column $i + 1$ and zeros elsewhere, and whose last row is…
nodes.title: Linear recurrences via powers of the companion matrix

nodes.summary: Let $S : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$ satisfy $S(0) = 1$, $S(1) = S(2) = 2$, $S(3) = 3$ and $S(m) = S(m - 1) + S(m - 2) - S(m - 3) + S(m - 4)$ for every $m \ge 4$. Then for every natural number $n$, the sum $\sum_{k=0}^{n} \bigl(\binom{n+5k}{2k}\binom{n}{k} \bmod 2\bigr)$ equals the value at $n$ of the run length transform of $S$.
nodes.title: Sum of $\binom{n+5k}{2k}\binom{n}{k} \bmod 2$ as a run length transform

nodes.summary: Let $S : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$ satisfy $S(0) = S(1) = S(2) = S(3) = 1$ and $S(m) = S(m - 1) + S(m - 2) - S(m - 3) + S(m - 4)$ for every $m \ge 4$. Then for every natural number $n$, the sum $\sum_{k=0}^{n} \bigl(\binom{n+5k}{2n+2k}\binom{n}{k} \bmod 2\bigr)$ equals the value at $n$ of the run length transform of $S$.
nodes.title: Sum of $\binom{n+5k}{2n+2k}\binom{n}{k} \bmod 2$ as a run length transform

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the sum $\sum_{k=0}^{n} \bigl(\binom{n+7k}{3n+k}\binom{n}{k} \bmod 2\bigr)$ equals the value at $n$ of the run length transform of the shifted Padovan sequence $P$, given by $P(0) = 1$, $P(1) = 0$, $P(2) = 1$ and $P(i + 3) = P(i + 1) + P(i)$, that is, $1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, \dots$ (the Padovan numbers, OEIS A000931, from offset $3$).
nodes.title: Sum of $\binom{n+7k}{3n+k}\binom{n}{k} \bmod 2$ as a run length transform

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the sum $\sum_{k=0}^{n} \bigl(\binom{n+k}{n-k}\binom{n}{k} \bmod 2\bigr)$ equals the value at $n$ of the run length transform of the sequence $S(i) = i + 1$ of positive integers $1, 2, 3, \dots$.
nodes.title: Sum of $\binom{n+k}{n-k}\binom{n}{k} \bmod 2$ as a run length transform

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the sum $\sum_{k=0}^{n} \bigl(\binom{n+3k}{6k}\binom{n}{k} \bmod 2\bigr)$ equals the value at $n$ of the run length transform of the sequence $S(i) = \lfloor i / 2 \rfloor + 1$ of doubled positive integers $1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, \dots$.
nodes.title: Sum of $\binom{n+3k}{6k}\binom{n}{k} \bmod 2$ as a run length transform

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the sum $\sum_{k=0}^{n} \bigl(\binom{n+2k}{2n-k}\binom{n}{k} \bmod 2\bigr)$ equals the value at $n$ of the run length transform of the sequence $S$ with $S(0) = S(1) = 1$ and $S(i) = L_{i-2}$ for $i \ge 2$, where $L_0 = 2, L_1 = 1, L_2 = 3, \dots$ are the Lucas numbers; that is, $S$ is $1, 1, 2, 1, 3, 4, 7, 11, \dots$.
nodes.title: Sum of $\binom{n+2k}{2n-k}\binom{n}{k} \bmod 2$ as a run length transform

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the sum $\sum_{k=0}^{n} \bigl(\binom{n+2k}{2k}\binom{n}{k} \bmod 2\bigr)$ equals the value at $n$ of the run length transform of the sequence $S$ with $S(0) = 1$ and $S(i) = 2$ for $i \ge 1$, that is, $1, 2, 2, 2, \dots$.
nodes.title: Sum of $\binom{n+2k}{2k}\binom{n}{k} \bmod 2$ as a run length transform

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be the run length transform of the periodic sequence $S$ with $S(i) = 0$ if $i \equiv 2 \pmod 3$ and $S(i) = 1$ otherwise, i.e. of $1, 1, 0, 1, 1, 0, \dots$. Then for every natural number $n$, $\sum_{k=0}^{n} \left(\binom{8k - 2n}{n + k} \binom{n}{k} \bmod 2\right) = T(n)$, where a binomial coefficient $\binom{a}{b}$ with $a < 0$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Rampersad–Wiebe Theorem 15

nodes.summary: Let $(p_j)_{j \ge 0}$ be the shifted Padovan sequence, $p_0 = 1$, $p_1 = 0$, $p_2 = 1$ and $p_{j+3} = p_{j+1} + p_j$, and let $T$ be the run length transform of $S(i) = p_{i+2}$, i.e. of $1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 5, \dots$ (the Padovan numbers, OEIS A000931, from offset $5$). Then for every natural number $n$, $\sum_{k=0}^{n} \left(\binom{7k - n}{n + k} \binom{n}{k} \bmod 2\right) = T(n)$, where a binomial coefficient…
nodes.title: Rampersad–Wiebe Theorem 12

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be the run length transform of the sequence $S$ with $S(i) = 1$ for even $i$ and $S(i) = (i + 1)/2$ for odd $i$, i.e. of $1, 1, 1, 2, 1, 3, 1, 4, \dots$. Then for every natural number $n$, $\sum_{k=0}^{n} \left(\binom{6k}{n + 3k} \binom{n}{k} \bmod 2\right) = T(n)$.
nodes.title: Rampersad–Wiebe Theorem 14

nodes.summary: Let $(N_j)_{j \ge 0}$ be Narayana's cows sequence, $N_0 = 0$, $N_1 = N_2 = 1$ and $N_j = N_{j-1} + N_{j-3}$ for $j \ge 3$, and let $T$ be the run length transform of $S(i) = N_{i+1}$, i.e. of $1, 1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, \dots$. Then for every natural number $n$, $\sum_{k=0}^{n} \left(\binom{n - k}{6k} \binom{n}{k} \bmod 2\right) = T(n)$.
nodes.title: Rampersad–Wiebe Theorem 7

nodes.summary: Let $(F_j)_{j \ge 0}$ be the Fibonacci numbers, $F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$, and let $T$ be the run length transform of $S(i) = F_{i+1}$, i.e. of $1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, \dots$. Then for every natural number $n$, $\sum_{k=0}^{n} \left(\binom{n - k}{2k} \binom{n}{k} \bmod 2\right) = T(n)$.
nodes.title: Rampersad–Wiebe Theorem 2

nodes.summary: Let $(F_j)_{j \ge 0}$ be the Fibonacci numbers, $F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$, and let $T$ be the run length transform of $S(i) = F_{i+2}$, i.e. of $1, 2, 3, 5, 8, \dots$. Then for every natural number $n$, $\sum_{k=0}^{n} \left(\binom{3k}{k} \binom{n}{k} \bmod 2\right) = T(n)$.
nodes.title: Rampersad–Wiebe Theorem 3

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be the run length transform of the sequence $S$ with $S(0) = 1$ and $S(i) = 2^{i-1}$ for $i \ge 1$, i.e. of $1, 1, 2, 4, 8, \dots$. Then for every natural number $n$, $\sum_{k=0}^{n} \left(\binom{n}{2k} \binom{n}{k} \bmod 2\right) = T(n)$.
nodes.title: Rampersad–Wiebe Theorem 4

nodes.summary: For every sequence $S : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$, the run length transform $T$ of $S$ satisfies $T(11) = S(1) S(2)$: in binary $11$ is $1011$, whose maximal runs of $1$s have lengths $2$ and $1$.
nodes.title: Run length transform at eleven

nodes.title: Run length transform of a linear recurrence (Rampersad–Wiebe Theorem 1)

nodes.summary: For every sequence $S : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$, the run length transform of $S$ takes the value $1$ at $0$, since $0$ has no runs of $1$s in binary.
nodes.title: Run length transform at zero

nodes.summary: For a sequence $S : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$, the run length transform of $S$ is the sequence $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$ given by $T(n) = \prod_{\ell \in \mathcal{L}(n)} S(\ell)$, where $\mathcal{L}(n)$ is the list of the lengths of the maximal runs of $1$s in the binary expansion of $n$, so that each run contributes one factor.
nodes.title: Run length transform

Number Theory

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
